subject: Post-demo: ApexHealth tech qualification — egress, mTLS, SDK auth checklist

Subject: Post-demo: ApexHealth tech qualification — egress, mTLS, SDK auth checklist

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo slot today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the PoC and timeline: 

Summary of what we covered
- Use case: in-app summarization + embeddings + reranker to power provider notes search and structured question answering.
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Private (VPC endpoint) with strict egress controls; backup to hosted model in failover scenarios.
- Integration surface: frontend calls your backend -> backend calls Redwood SDK or Private endpoint.

Open technical items (we need answers to these to size the config and produce a checklist):
1) Egress model: do you require that all outbound traffic from your ingestion/transform cluster be forced through a NAT gateway owned by Apex, or can we rely on PrivateLink-style VPC endpoint to avoid public egress? Provide preferred approach.
2) IP allowlist: please confirm whether your security team can accept CIDR ranges (we'll supply Redwood egress CIDRs) or you require individual IPs. Also confirm whether IPv6 is needed.
3) DNS resolution: will your private DNS resolve our private endpoint hostnames (we can provide split-horizon names), or do you prefer ip-based endpoints?
4) mTLS: do you want mutual TLS for all control-plane and data-plane connections, or just mTLS for the VPC connector? Are you able to provision client certs via your internal PKI, or should we provide short-lived certs?
5) SDK auth pattern: preferred pattern is ephemeral API key + short TTL rotated by your backend (we provide a rotation guide). Do you need HMAC-signed requests instead?
6) Structured output/tool calling: confirm whether your backend will accept structured JSON with a strict schema from the model or whether you need a verification/reranking step server-side.

Attachments: I attached a short networking checklist and our ephemeral key rotation guide. I will follow up with a proposed PoC checklist and timeline once we get answers above.

Next steps proposed
- Samir: confirm #1-#6 and attach a copy of ApexHealth's network policy (CIDRs, DNS practice, PKI contact).
- Redwood: schedule infra deep-dive (1 hour) with your NetOps and App infra — propose Wed 29th or Thu 30th.
- Redwood SE (Ben): prepare a deterministic embedding + rerank demo that uses your sample data schema.

Thanks — Rishi

--

Rishi — thanks, useful summary. Quick answers from NetOps below and a couple of follow-ups. Forwarding their note here.

NetOps initial answers (copied from netops@apexhealth.com)
- Egress: Prefer PrivateLink (no public egress) if you can provide an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. If not, we can accept a fixed egress NAT with your listed CIDRs.
- IP allowlist: We accept CIDR ranges; pref /24 blocks preferred. IPv6 not required at this time.
- DNS: We operate split-horizon for private names; we can consume a private-zone A record.
- mTLS: We prefer mTLS for data-plane; we currently operate an internal PKI and can issue client certs. We will need your guidance on cert lifetimes and rotation.
- SDK auth: Ephemeral API keys are preferred. We will not accept long-lived, embedded keys in browser clients.
- Structured output: We need the model to emit a stable JSON envelope for the QA response; we will run server-side verification and a light reranker based on domain heuristics.

Attachments: attached "apexhealth-networking-reqs.pdf" with additional firewall rules and our accepted cipher suites.

Follow-ups/questions from ApexHealth
1) For PrivateLink, do you require cross-account VPC peering, or can Redwood publish an endpoint service that we consume in our account?
2) For mutual TLS, can Redwood accept client certs signed by our CA, or do you require mutual provisioning?

Happy to take the infra deep-dive. Wed 29th 10:00am PT works for the team.

— Samir

Samir — quick technical notes from SE side to help the deep-dive agenda: 

PrivateLink vs NAT: we can support both. PrivateLink (AWS NLB + endpoint service) is our recommended path for zero public egress and better DNS hygiene. When using PrivateLink we publish a service name; your side will create the endpoint in your VPC. No cross-account peering required beyond the VPC endpoint connection.

mTLS and certs: we support two flows:
- Customer-supplied client certs (signed by your CA) — we validate client cert chain on the Redwood side and map certificate SAN to a customer identity.
- Redwood-provisioned short-lived client certs (30–90 min TTL) with automated rotation via our control plane.

Ephemeral keys: recommended pattern — backend requests short-lived token from Redwood auth service over mTLS, then use token for SDK calls. The token TTL is configurable; default 15m. We will share the ephemeral key guide in the drive link.

Structured output: our structured-output tool-calling mode can emit a constrained JSON schema; we also provide a server-side verifier lib (open-source) to validate schema before applying changes. For reranking: we can run an embeddings-based reranker in your VPC endpoint or return embeddings to your server for rerank — both are supported.

I'll prepare a short diagram and checklist for the deep-dive.

- Ben
